features.name: capital_run_log_total
features.description: Log-transformed total capital run length to compress heavy right skew, making threshold splits more effective for tree models
features.expected_model_benefit: Compresses extreme outliers in capital run total, enabling cleaner splits on moderate vs high capital usage

features.name: capital_run_longest_log
features.description: Log-transformed longest capital run length to handle extreme values up to 9989
features.expected_model_benefit: Enables better splits on longest capital sequence, a strong spam indicator when very large

features.name: capital_avg_to_longest_ratio
features.description: Ratio of average capital run length to longest capital run length, capturing burstiness of capitalization
features.expected_model_benefit: Low ratio indicates one very long burst of caps; high ratio indicates uniformly capitalized text - both patterns differ from normal email

features.name: exclamation_dollar_combined
features.description: Sum of exclamation mark frequency (char_freq_4) and dollar sign frequency (char_freq_3), both strong spam indicators
features.expected_model_benefit: Combined signal of two highly spam-correlated punctuation characters; tree can split on combined threshold

features.name: dollar_sign_present
features.description: Boolean indicator for presence of dollar sign character (char_freq_3 > 0)
features.expected_model_benefit: Direct boolean split on dollar sign presence, a classic spam indicator for financial solicitations

features.name: high_capital_burst_flag
features.description: Boolean flag for emails with very long capital runs (longest > 20), indicating aggressive capitalization typical of spam
features.expected_model_benefit: Direct boolean split capturing emails with extreme capitalization bursts, a strong spam signal

features.name: spam_word_cluster_score
features.description: Weighted sum of high-frequency spam-associated word features: word_freq_18 (your), word_freq_20 (free), word_freq_24 (business), word_freq_26 (remove), word_freq_44 (credit)
features.expected_model_benefit: Aggregates multiple spam-associated word frequencies into a single score for efficient tree splitting

features.name: nonzero_word_count
features.description: Count of word frequency features that are non-zero, measuring vocabulary diversity of the email
features.expected_model_benefit: Spam emails often use a narrow set of trigger words; low nonzero count with high individual frequencies is a spam pattern

features.name: capital_intensity_bucket
features.description: Ordinal bucket for capital run total: 0=low (<=50), 1=medium (51-200), 2=high (201-500), 3=very high (>500)
features.expected_model_benefit: Ordinal encoding of capital intensity allows tree to make clean threshold splits at meaningful boundaries

features.name: special_char_total_freq
features.description: Sum of all character frequency features (char_freq_0 through char_freq_5), measuring overall special character density
features.expected_model_benefit: High special character density is a strong spam signal; aggregated feature reduces dimensionality while preserving signal
features.formula: char_freq_0 + char_freq_1 + char_freq_2 + char_freq_3 + char_freq_4 + char_freq_5

features.name: word_freq_concentration
features.description: Semantic assessment of how concentrated word frequencies are in a few high-frequency terms vs spread across many moderate-frequency terms. Score 1-5: 1=very spread/diverse vocabulary, 3=moderate concentration, 5=highly concentrated in few words. Spam tends toward high concentration.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures vocabulary concentration pattern that distinguishes template-like spam from natural email prose

features.name: aggressive_solicitation_score
features.description: Semantic score 0-4 for how many aggressive solicitation signals are present: dollar signs present (+1), exclamation marks present (+1), very high capital runs (+1), multiple spam-associated words present (+1). Higher score indicates more aggressive solicitation style.
features.expected_model_benefit: Combines multiple spam-style signals into an ordinal score that tree models can split on efficiently
